html:
Michael Manley was prime minister of Jamaica from 1972 to 1980 and again from 1989 to 1992. The son of Norman Manley, he led the People's National Party.

In the 1970s he pursued democratic socialism: a minimum wage, free education, land reform and a levy on foreign bauxite firms. He was friendly with Fidel Castro and spoke for the poor countries of the world.

The economy shrank, capital fled, and the 1980 election was fought with guns between party gangs; about 800 people were killed. He lost to Edward Seaga. Returning in 1989, he followed market policies. Bob Marley tried to bring the parties together at the One Love Peace Concert of 1978.
sum: Michael Manley was prime minister of Jamaica from 1972 to 1980 and again from 1989 to 1992. The son of Norman Manley, he led the People's National Party.
